newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares broadly weaker on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares broadly weaker on fund sales.

text.p: Singapore share prices were broadly weaker at noon on Thursday threatening to drift lower on a lack of institutional interest, dealers said.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was adjusted to account for Keppel Corp's one-for-four bonus issue phased in on Thursday. During the lunchtime break, the index clawed back to 2,018.56 from an early low of 2,000.44.
"It was a false start because the ex-bonus issue wasn't factored in," one U.S. investment house dealer said.
But he said liquidation of heavyweights such as banks and property issues could drag the market down further.
Keppel's theorectical ex-bonus price was S$6.92, but the share traded below that to S$6.80. It closed at S$8.65 on Wednesday.
Japanese investors were leading sellers of Keppel and other stocks as they reallocated funds to other markets, dealers said.
Foreign tranches of banks like DBS fell 40 cents to S$17.10, OUB slipped 30 cents to S$9.65. Property issues City Development eased 50 cents to S$12.40 and Parkway, down 10 cents to S$6.25.
Overall volume was thin at 50.5 million shares with market breadth weak as losers beat gainers 209 to 60.
